args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The service was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service reports healthy with a 0.2% error rate. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 was promoted. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failures and review why an unhealthy staging release went to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is passing health checks again.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1, the latest deploy, was failing health checks in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. Since the rollback, the service reports healthy with a 0.2% error rate.
- **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovered health and error rate. It also suggests next steps: find out why v2.3.1 failed and why it was released.

The release history shows that the v2.3.1 test build was also unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 went to production. I noted this in the incident. It's worth checking how it got past that check.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
